subject: Encryption / KMS options - followup (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@acmehealth.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-26T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Encryption / KMS options - followup

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and next steps so we’re all aligned: 

High-level requirements we heard
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ (pref TLS 1.3) for all API traffic; desire for mTLS on private connections
- At-rest: AES-256 encrypted model+request stores; option for customer-managed keys (CMEK) or HSM-backed keys
- Key management: ability to bring your own key (BYOK) via AWS KMS / CloudHSM or customer HSM for on-prem deployments
- Multi-tenant isolation: per-customer keying/isolation for prod data is preferred
- Logging & audit: request-level audit logs (who/when/request id), ability to redact PII in logs, and log forwarding to customer account for long-term retention
- Data residency & retention: primary region us-east-1; retention policy must be configurable (default 30 days; need ability to hold up to 7+ years for compliance)

Open items / clarifications needed from Acme (action items)
- Confirm whether Acme requires HSM (FIPS) for all keys or KMS CMEK is sufficient
- Desired log retention window and whether logs must be exported to Acme account immediately
- Any specific regulatory controls (PCI, HIPAA, HITRUST) beyond SOC2 we should map against

What we’re sending you (attached / links)
- Redwood_KMS_Options.pdf — detailed options for CMEK, CloudHSM, and on-prem HSM integrations
- SOC2_summary_2025.pdf — high-level SOC2 scope and control areas for our hosted and private offerings
- Acme_SOW_draft.docx — initial SOW template with enterprise private deployment options (draft)

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with Rishi (infra) to discuss CMEK/CloudHSM architecture and per-customer key isolation — can do this week.
2) Share any compliance requirements or standard questionnaire (if you have one) so we can map controls.
3) If you’re interested in Dedicated/Private deployment, we’ll follow up with deployment options and estimated timeline/cost.

Suggested 30–45min slots (PST):
- Thu 2026-02-26 3:00pm, Fri 2026-02-27 10:00am, Fri 2026-02-27 2:00pm

If any of those don’t work, happy to adjust.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0183

From: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-02-26T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Encryption / KMS options - followup

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few immediate clarifications from our side: 

- HSM vs KMS: Acme’s security team has a hard preference for HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2/3). Is CloudHSM supported for the hosted path, or would that require a private deployment?
- Per-customer keys: we need strong isolation. Ideally each Acme tenant would have a dedicated key we control. Can Redwood support per-customer CMEK or is that only in the Dedicated/Private model?
- Audit logs: we want the ability to push detailed audit logs (including request IDs and token hashes) into our logging account and retain for 7 years. Can you confirm whether logs can be exported to our cloud account, and whether PII redaction is automated or requires custom configuration?
- On-prem key option: for our on-prem teams, would BYOK allow us to keep keys entirely within our HSM?

Also — please confirm which of the proposed slots Rishi can do; 2pm Friday would be ideal for us.

Appreciate the attachments — I’ll review and circle back with the security team.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Thompson
Senior Security Architect | Acme Health
alex.thompson@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@acmehealth.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-27T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Encryption / KMS options - followup

Alex — thanks, great questions. Answers below and next steps.

1) CloudHSM / HSM support
- Hosted API: we support CMEK via AWS KMS for hosted customers. CloudHSM integration (customer HSM instances) is supported when customers want HSM-backed keys; for fully managed CloudHSM-backed keys we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments to meet FIPS requirements and ensure exclusivity.
- Private / On-prem: full BYOK with customer HSM is supported in our Private deployment; keys remain inside customer HSM and Redwood performs envelope encryption. We can document key lifecycle and access patterns for your security review.

2) Per-customer keys / key isolation
- We support per-customer CMEK and per-tenant keying in Dedicated and Private modes. For hosted customers we can enable per-customer KMS keys (when you bring the key into your cloud account and grant Redwood the minimal rights) — that gives strong isolation while preserving a hosted experience.

3) Audit logs & retention
- Audit logs include request id, timestamp, model, route, non-sensitive metadata, and an optional token-hash field. PII redaction: we provide redaction tools at ingest (configurable rules) and can also support a sampling-based approach for troubleshooting.
- Export: logs can be exported to your cloud account (CloudWatch / S3 / Stackdriver) via cross-account delivery for long-term retention. Default retention is 30 days in our platform; we can configure exports to your account for 7+ years per Acme policy.

4) On-prem BYOK
- Yes — in Private deployments your HSM can hold the root key; Redwood uses envelope encryption and does not persist your unwrapped key. We’ll provide an architecture diagram and HSM integration guide in the attachments.

Attached: Redwood_KMS_Options.pdf (detailed options + architecture), SOC2_summary_2025.pdf, Acme_SOW_draft.docx

Next steps
- Rishi and I can run the technical deep-dive Friday 2026-02-27 at 2:00pm PST — Rishi, does that work?
- If that looks good, we’ll put together a short security appendix mapping SOC2 controls to your questionnaire and present key rotation and key-access procedures.
- I’ll also surface the HSM/CMEK details to our infra team and prepare a short demo of key lifecycle (how we use KMS, where keys live, and how we forward logs).

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference
